verdict: CONFIRMED: shared first-dispatch refusal prematurely retires a different tab unresolved dispatch of identical reserved ID/body
scope: Exact existing workbench plus classification controller, independent two-context scenario over qualified atomic transaction helper and serialized Web Locks. No backend/provider claims simulated as actual model executions.
cause: Claim previous is local/durable pending at claim time, but first dispatch captures null. Second tab dispatches same reserved body before first response. First handler 4xx cleanup does not know another tab owns unresolved HTTP transport. Its exact-body CAS passes and writes authoritative retirement marker.
design_feedback: Nonqueued exclusive origin dispatch lock before Claim held through HTTP settlement and cleanup; every ClearStorage obtains it or accepts only live private owner capability; dispatch -> storage -> IDB lock ordering; no queued retry/cleanup. Keep exact body on ambiguous acknowledgments and after crash/reload; preserve CAS.
qualification_needed: Two-tab same-ID held first POST: second explicit submit refuses with zero POST and no queued retry after lock release.
Matching summary or exact GET from another tab cannot retire pending while first transport remains held.
Lost ACK, page close/crash, reload: pending exact body survives; explicit same-ID retry allowed and subsequent 4xx retains it.
Sole fresh definite refusal permits corrected/new intent; no queued stale cleanup can delete successor.
ifAvailable true missing/busy lock semantics tested using actual native Web Locks and realistic null-capable mock.
limitations: This is a deterministic bounded VM reproduction; actual HTTP admission count and native browser reproduction are assigned separately by parent.
